---
title: 'Thanh Local End-to-End Environment'
description: 'Run the isolated Supabase stack, web, Playwright and mobile simulator/emulator end-to-end tests on the Thanh Mac Studio.'
updatedAt: '2026-10-24'
---

The Thanh Mac Studio (`ssh skr-studio`) hosts a repeatable local end-to-end
environment: an isolated Supabase project with migrations and seed data, the
`apps/web` dev server, Playwright, and the mobile app on a dedicated iOS
Simulator and Android Emulator. Use it to validate changes against real
simulator/emulator runs instead of host-only widget tests.

The entry point is `scripts/thanh-e2e/thanh-e2e.mjs`. It works on any macOS host
with the same toolchain; Thanh defaults are baked in and overridable by
environment variables.

<Warning>
  Use Thanh only for this lane. Queue heavy steps (`up`, `seed`, `web`,
  `web-e2e`, `mobile-e2e`) with `ttr resources run --` from a checkout under
  `/Users/thanh/ci-lanes/tuturuuu-*`, and never stop Upskii or other lanes'
  containers, emulators or queue owners.
</Warning>

Android's dummy Firebase input is created exclusively: an existing file or
symlink is preserved, including a dangling symlink. PID state is opened without
following symlinks and classified and read through the same descriptor; malformed
PID values are ignored, while unsafe file types fail explicitly. Run the focused
filesystem regressions with `node --test scripts/thanh-e2e/*.test.mjs`; no simulator
or database setup is required.

## Toolchain

Everything Tuturuuu-specific lives in user space under
`/Users/thanh/ci-lanes/tuturuuu-tools` (`$T`). Source `$T/mobile-env.sh` first;
it sets `DEVELOPER_DIR`, `JAVA_HOME`, `ANDROID_HOME`/`ANDROID_AVD_HOME`,
`PUB_CACHE`, `GRADLE_USER_HOME`, an isolated `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` for Flutter
settings, and `PATH` (Flutter 3.47.7, Temurin 17, Android SDK tools, Bun,
Docker).

| Component | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Xcode 26.5 + iOS 26.5 runtime | `/Applications/Xcode.app` |
| Flutter 3.47.7 | `$T/flutter-3.47.7-stable-arm64/flutter` |
| JDK 17 (Temurin) | `$T/jdk` |
| Android SDK (platforms 36 + 37, NDK 28.2, API 36 arm64 image) | `$T/android-sdk` |
| AVDs | `$T/android-avd` |
| E2E state (Supabase workdir, env files, logs, screenshots) | `$T/e2e/<project>` |

`xcode-select` on Thanh still points at the Command Line Tools. Dart
native-asset build hooks run with a filtered environment that keeps `PATH` but
drops `DEVELOPER_DIR`, so `$T/bin/xcrun` pins Xcode. Without it, iOS builds fail
in `objective_c/hook/build.dart` with `Bad state: No element`. Remove the shim
after an administrator runs
`sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`.

## Isolation

| Resource | Value | Override |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supabase project id | `tuturuuu-e2e` | `TUTURUUU_E2E_PROJECT_ID` |
| Supabase ports | `8000`-`8007` (API `8001`, DB `8002`, Studio `8003`, mail `8004`) | `TUTURUUU_E2E_SUPABASE_BASE_PORT` |
| Web dev server | `http://127.0.0.1:7803` | `TUTURUUU_E2E_WEB_PORT` |
| Satellites | Calendar on `http://localhost:7806` | `TUTURUUU_E2E_SATELLITES` (`calendar`, `none`) |
| iOS Simulator | `tuturuuu-ios-iphone17pro` | `TUTURUUU_E2E_IOS_SIM` |
| Android Emulator | `tuturuuu-android-36-pixel9pro` on `emulator-5580` | `TUTURUUU_E2E_AVD`, `TUTURUUU_E2E_AVD_PORT` |

The ports stay canonical on purpose: the web local-E2E auth and captcha bypass
(`apps/web/src/lib/auth/local-e2e.ts`) and the Playwright safety guard
(`apps/web/e2e/helpers/environment.ts`) only trust Supabase `:8001` and web
`:7803` on loopback. With other ports, mobile password sign-in fails with
`Turnstile is not configured`. Isolation comes from the project id instead: the
script refuses the default `tuturuuu` id and `up` fails fast when any port in
the block is already listening, so it never adopts another lane's stack. Only
one stack on the canonical ports can run on a host at a time; stop it with
`down` when you finish. The Supabase config is staged from tracked
`apps/database/supabase` files and rewritten with the isolated helpers from
`apps/database/scripts/run-supabase-isolated.js`.

Docker over SSH cannot use the macOS keychain (`credsStore: desktop`). The
script points `DOCKER_CONFIG` at a credential-free directory in the state dir
and `DOCKER_HOST` at the Docker Desktop socket, so public image pulls work
anonymously and the keychain is never touched.

## Run it

```bash
ssh skr-studio
. ~/ci-lanes/tuturuuu-tools/mobile-env.sh
cd ~/ci-lanes/tuturuuu-e2e          # any checkout under ci-lanes/tuturuuu-*
bun install                         # once per checkout
E2E=scripts/thanh-e2e/thanh-e2e.mjs

node $E2E doctor
ttr resources run -- node $E2E up          # start + migrations + seed
ttr resources run -- node $E2E web         # build types/supabase, start web + satellites
node $E2E devices                          # boot simulator + emulator headless
ttr resources run -- node $E2E web-e2e --install -- e2e/auth.noauth.spec.ts
ttr resources run -- node $E2E mobile-e2e ios
ttr resources run -- node $E2E mobile-e2e android
ttr resources run -- node $E2E mobile-e2e android --mode=profile
node $E2E status
node $E2E down            # stop web + Supabase; --web-only, --purge
```

`seed` re-applies migrations and seed data. `env` rewrites
`$T/e2e/<project>/env/web.env` and `mobile.json` from `supabase status`.
`web.log` and other logs live in the state dir's `logs/`.

## Test accounts

The seed creates `local@tuturuuu.com` (root admin) and `user1`-`user4@tuturuuu.com`
with the public local-only seed password from `apps/database/supabase/seed.sql`.
The mobile flow defaults to `local@tuturuuu.com`; override with
`--dart-define=E2E_EMAIL=...` only for other seeded accounts.

## Satellites

Web proxies some owner APIs to satellite apps; Calendar's event API is proxied
to the Calendar app, so without it Agenda shows `ApiException(500): Request
failed` and web logs `Failed to proxy https://calendar.tuturuuu.localhost/...
ECONNREFUSED`. `web` therefore also starts each satellite in
`TUTURUUU_E2E_SATELLITES` (default `calendar`) on its default port with the
same local Supabase env and `WEB_APP_URL`/`INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN` pointing
back at web; web gets `CALENDAR_APP_URL=http://localhost:7806`. `down` stops
web and satellites. `web` also builds `@tuturuuu/internal-api`, which Calendar
imports from `dist/`.

Satellites run on their Next.js runtime (`next dev`), not Vite+ `dev:app`.
Vite+ dev runs Calendar inside workerd, which loads linked workspace packages
unbundled; `@tuturuuu/internal-api` builds as CommonJS (`NodeNext` without
`"type": "module"`), so startup fails with `ReferenceError: exports is not
defined`, or `Failed to resolve entry for package "@tuturuuu/internal-api"`
before it is built. The Next runtime serves the same route handlers.

## Mobile wiring

`mobile.json` is passed with `--dart-define-from-file` and routes
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and every `*_API_BASE_URL` owner to loopback
`127.0.0.1`. Android permits cleartext only to `127.0.0.1`/`localhost`, and the
app rewrites `localhost` to `10.0.2.2`, so the script uses `127.0.0.1` and runs
`adb reverse` for the web and Supabase ports. All satellite API owners point at
the local web server, which owns the live API handlers.

`apps/mobile/integration_test/e2e_flows_test.dart` signs in with the seeded
account, opens Agenda, opens Settings → Preferences, changes the personal
timezone (default `Pacific/Niue`, override with `--dart-define=E2E_TIMEZONE=...`;
pick a zone near the top of the picker, whose list is lazy and lives in a
draggable sheet) and returns to Agenda. It fails if an `ErrorWidget` renders at any
step. At each checkpoint it prints an `E2E_SHOT <name>` marker and holds the
frame; the runner streams `flutter drive` output and captures the device with
`xcrun simctl io ... screenshot` or `adb exec-out screencap`, so screenshots
work in debug, profile and release builds. Shots and `flutter-drive.log` land
in `$T/e2e/<project>/shots/<platform>-<mode>-<timestamp>/`. (On Android,
`IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding.takeScreenshot` after
`convertFlutterSurfaceToImage` captured only the first frame.)

Before each run the script prepares the gitignored Firebase inputs the same way
mobile CI does: `scripts/mobile-deployment/firebase-service-config.py` copies the
tracked development plist on iOS, and Android gets the synthetic
`google-services.json` CI writes. iOS builds run `pod install`, which can leave
`ios/Podfile.lock` and `project.pbxproj` modified in the E2E checkout; do not
commit those side effects.

`flutter test -d <device> test/...` does not run on the device: files outside
`integration_test/` run on the host VM. Widget tests that resize
`tester.view` also fail under the live binding, so on-device coverage belongs in
`integration_test/`.

## Release-mode gray screen

Release builds replace the debug red error box with a gray `ErrorWidget`. iOS
simulators run debug builds only (Flutter refuses `--profile` and `--release`),
so reproduce release-only rendering on the Android emulator with
`mobile-e2e android --mode=profile` or `--mode=release`. The same `ErrorWidget`
assertion reports the failing screen, and the screenshots show it.

## Web Playwright

`web` and `web-e2e` set `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7803`, the local Supabase
keys and `TUTURUUU_LOCAL_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS=1`, the same local-only opt-in CI web
E2E uses. `local-e2e.ts` honors it only for the loopback `:7803`/`:8001`
origins; without it the `/api/auth/dev-session` rate-limit reset returns 403
and most auth specs fail in `beforeEach`. `--install` installs the
Playwright Chromium build first. Pass spec paths or Playwright flags after `--`.

## Gotchas

- Browsers must open web at `http://localhost:7803`, not `127.0.0.1`: Next dev
  serves its dev resources (HMR, hydration) only to `localhost`, so a
  `127.0.0.1` page stays unhydrated and the login form remains disabled. The
  script uses `localhost` for `BASE_URL`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL` and keeps
  `127.0.0.1` for mobile, which Android cleartext requires.
- `bootstrap()` installs the app's `FlutterError.onError`. The integration test
  restores the test binding's handler after `app.main()`; otherwise a framework
  error surfaces only as `A test overrode FlutterError.onError ...` and the real
  failure is hidden.
- Mobile login ignores "Continue with email" while OTP availability resolves
  (a short grace period); the test retries the tap until the password stage
  renders.
- Every wait in the flow captures `timeout-<label>.png` and prints the visible
  text on timeout, so a failing run shows the stuck screen.
- Simulator and emulator keyboards are real: the test dismisses the keyboard
  before tapping, and re-enters the email before each Continue attempt because
  the login page can rebuild once startup checks settle. On the Android
  profile build the typed email still did not stick; after 20 seconds the test
  signs in through `AuthCubit.signInWithPassword` (the call the Sign in button
  makes) and logs `E2E_NOTE`, so profile mode still covers Agenda and Settings.
- `mobile-e2e` runs `flutter drive` in its own process group with a 20-minute
  timeout and requires the `All tests passed` line; a killed drive can exit 0.

- The web auth spam guard blocks requests without a native or browser user
  agent; probe mobile APIs with a `Dart/3.x (dart:io)` user agent, not bare
  `curl`.
- A killed `flutter run`/`flutter drive` can leave `adb ... logcat` or
  `simctl ... log stream` children holding stdout open, which pins a
  `ttr resources` slot. Kill only your own leftover streamer.
- `permission_handler_android` compiles against Android SDK 37; keep
  `platforms;android-37.0` installed.
- Plain `./gradlew` tasks need `-Ptarget=lib/main_development.dart` because the
  app has no `lib/main.dart`, and flavored task names such as
  `:app:testDevelopmentDebugUnitTest`.

## Measuring Vite+ satellites signed in

Production Meet and Mail redirect every signed-out request to the web login,
so first-load metrics for their real surfaces need a signed-in session. The
same isolated stack serves that: build the satellite on Thanh against the local
Supabase values from `env/web.env` (`vp build` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:<port>`
and `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL=http://localhost:7803` exported, because the client
bundle inlines them), then `vp preview --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>` runs the
emitted Worker in workerd. Three details make the handshake work:

- Void copies only the `secrets.required` entries of `void.config.ts` into
  `dist/server/.dev.vars`. Meet therefore has no
  `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` after a build; append it (and the loopback
  `WEB_APP_URL`/`INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN`) before starting the preview, or the
  Worker cannot verify the app-session cookie web issues.
- Supabase cookies are only trusted on `*.tuturuuu.com` and
  `*.tuturuuu.localhost` hosts. On plain `localhost` the web session cookie is
  host-only and reaches every port, and `/verify-token` then clears it with
  `response.cookies.set`, which rebuilds the `Set-Cookie` header and drops the
  app-session cookies that were appended a moment earlier. Sign in on web,
  capture the `/verify-token?token=…` URL web redirects to, clear the `sb-*`
  cookies from the browser context, and only then open that URL on the
  satellite origin.
- Keep the Playwright run on `ttr resources run --` and point it at the
  `playwright` package under `~/ci-lanes/tuturuuu-e2e/node_modules/.bun`; the
  Chromium build in `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright` is shared.

The satellite then serves `/personal/…` with a real session, and a CDP-based
Playwright script can record TTFB, FCP, LCP, CLS and transferred JavaScript for
cold and warm loads of the exact local build.
